title: The spectral sequence of a filtered complex
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and let $K^\bullet$ be a complex equipped with a bounded decreasing filtration $F^\bullet K^\bullet$ by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. Put $X^{[p,q]}=F^pK^\bullet/F^qK^\bullet$ for $p\le q$. Then there is a cohomological spectral sequence $(E_r^{p,q},d_r)_{r\ge1}$ with $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(X^{[p,p+1]})=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet)$ and $d_r:E_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$; $d_1$ is the connecting map of $0\to X^{[p+1,p+2]}\to X^{[p,p+2]}\to X^{[p,p+1]}\to0$. For every $r\ge1$, inside $\operatorname{gr}^pK^{p+q}$, $Z_r^{p,q}=((F^pK^{p+q}\cap d^{-1}(F^{p+r}K^{p+q+1}))+F^{p+1}K^{p+q})/F^{p+1}K^{p+q}$ and $B_r^{p,q}=((F^pK^{p+q}\cap d(F^{p-r+1}K^{p+q-1}))+F^{p+1}K^{p+q})/F^{p+1}K^{p+q}$, with $B_r\subseteq Z_r$ and $E_r^{p,q}\cong Z_r^{p,q}/B_r^{p,q}$. Equivalently, the same object is naturally isomorphic to the image of $H^{p+q}(X^{[p,p+r]})\to H^{p+q}(X^{[p-r+1,p+1]})$ induced by the map $F^pK^\bullet/F^{p+r}K^\bullet\to F^{p-r+1}K^\bullet/F^{p+1}K^\bullet$. The induced image filtration on $H^n(K^\bullet)$ is finite and separated, and $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pH^{p+q}(K^\bullet)$, so the sequence converges [def-sp-convergence]. The construction is functorial. If $F^pK=K$ for $p\le0$ and $H^i(\operatorname{gr}^pK)=0$ outside $i\in[p,p+1]$, then $E_r^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\ge0$ and terms stabilize for $r>\max(p,q)+1$.

proof.text: For each finite filtered complex and r ≥ 1, construct the quotient transition F^p/F^(p+r) → F^(p-r+1)/F^(p+1) using cokernel.desc. The composite from F^(p+r) vanishes since p+1 ≤ p+r, by Subobject.ofLE_comp_ofLE and cokernel.condition. cokernel.π_desc gives the required equation; choose these maps simultaneously.

Apply the canonical-pages construction to these quotient transitions and their proved projection equation. Package its spectral-sequence functor, first-page and image comparisons and remaining properties together with the constructed transitions.

proof_origin.place: Canonical quotient transitions proved by the cokernel universal property; remaining construction in thm-sp-spectral-object-yields-canonical-pages.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and let $K^\bullet$ be a complex in
$\mathcal A$ equipped with a decreasing filtration
[def-sp-filtration] $F^\bullet K^\bullet$ by subcomplexes, with graded
pieces $\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet=F^pK^\bullet/F^{p+1}K^\bullet$. Then:

- (a) the long exact cohomology sequences of the short exact sequences
  $0\to F^{p+1}K^\bullet\to F^pK^\bullet\to\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet\to0$
  form an exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple] with
  $$
   D^{p,q}=H^{p+q}\bigl(F^pK^\bullet\bigr),\qquad
   E^{p,q}=H^{p+q}\bigl(\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet\bigr),
  $$
  $\alpha$ induced by the inclusions, $g$ by the projections and $f$ the
  connecting homomorphisms (bidegrees $(-1,+1)$, $(0,0)$, $(+1,0)$); its
  spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence] $\bigl(E_r^{p,q},d_r\bigr)_{r\geq1}$
  has
  $$
   E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}\bigl(\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet\bigr),
   \qquad
   d_r:E_r^{p,q}\longrightarrow E_r^{p+r,q-r+1},
  $$
  the differential $d_1$ being the composite of the connecting homomorphism
  $H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet)\to H^{p+q+1}(F^{p+1}K^\bullet)$ and
  of the projection
  $H^{p+q+1}(F^{p+1}K^\bullet)\to H^{p+q+1}(\operatorname{gr}^{p+1}K^\bullet)$;
- (b) if the filtration is *bounded*, that is, for every degree $n$ one has
  $F^pK^n=K^n$ for $p\ll0$ and $F^pK^n=0$ for $p\gg0$, then the induced
  filtration [def-sp-image-filtration]
  $F^pH^n(K^\bullet):=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(F^pK^\bullet)\to
  H^n(K^\bullet)\bigr)$ is finite and separated on each $H^n(K^\bullet)$, and
  the spectral sequence converges [def-sp-convergence] to it along the maps
  $H^{p+q}(F^pK^\bullet)\to H^{p+q}(K^\bullet)$; in particular
  $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pH^{p+q}(K^\bullet)$;
- (c) the construction is functorial in the pair
  $(K^\bullet,F^\bullet K^\bullet)$: a morphism of filtered complexes induces
  a morphism of the exact couples of (a), hence of the spectral sequences,
  and if it induces isomorphisms on the $E_1$-terms, then it induces
  isomorphisms on all pages [lem-sp-page-induction];
- (d) first-quadrant variant: if $E_1^{p,q}=0$ unless $p\geq0$ and $q\geq0$,
  then the pages $E_r$, $r\geq2$, form a first-quadrant cohomological
  spectral sequence whose entries stabilize for $r>\max(p,q+1)$; if moreover
  the filtration is bounded, with $F^0H^n(K^\bullet)=H^n(K^\bullet)$ and
  $F^{n+1}H^n(K^\bullet)=0$ for $n\geq0$, then by (b) this first-quadrant
  spectral sequence abuts to $\bigl(H^n(K^\bullet)\bigr)_{n\geq0}$ with the
  induced filtrations.

proof.text:
They assemble into an exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple] with
$D^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(F^pK^\bullet)$ and
$E^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet)$, the maps $\alpha,g,f$
having bidegrees $(-1,+1)$, $(0,0)$, $(+1,0)$; the exactness required of a
couple is exactly the exactness of these sequences.

Step 2: the pages. The spectral sequence of the couple, started at the page
$r_0=1$ ([def-sp-exact-couple]), is a spectral sequence
[def-sp-spectral-sequence] whose differentials $d_r=g_r\circ f_r$ have
bidegree $(+r,1-r)$. Its first page is $E_1=E$, and $d_1=g\circ f$ is the
connecting homomorphism followed by the projection, as stated in (a).

Step 3: convergence. Assume the filtration bounded and fix $n=p+q$. Then
$H^n(F^pK^\bullet)\to H^n(K^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism for $p\ll0$ (the
complexes agree in degrees $n-1,n,n+1$), and $H^n(F^pK^\bullet)=0$ for
$p\gg0$ (it is a subquotient of $F^pK^n=0$); hence $F^pH^n=H^n$ for $p\ll0$
and $F^pH^n=0$ for $p\gg0$, so the induced filtration is finite and
separated. In the couple, $E_r^{p,q}=Z_r/B_r$ with
$Z_r=f^{-1}(\operatorname{im}\alpha^{r-1})$ and
$B_r=g(\ker\alpha^{r-1})$ ([def-sp-convergence]). For $r$ large the source
$H^{n+1}(F^{p+r}K^\bullet)$ of $\alpha^{r-1}$ into $H^{n+1}(F^{p+1}K^\bullet)$
vanishes, so $Z_r=\ker f=\operatorname{im}g$, and
$\ker\bigl(\alpha^{r-1}:H^n(F^pK^\bullet)\to H^n(F^{p-r+1}K^\bullet)\bigr)$
is the kernel $\ker\iota$ of $\iota:H^n(F^pK^\bullet)\to H^n(K^\bullet)$; so
the differentials at $(p,q)$ vanish from then on, and

$$
 E_\infty^{p,q}=\frac{g\bigl(H^n(F^pK^\bullet)\bigr)}
 {g(\ker\iota)}\cong
 \frac{H^n(F^pK^\bullet)}{\ker\iota+\operatorname{im}\alpha}
 \cong\frac{\operatorname{im}\iota}{\iota(\operatorname{im}\alpha)}
 =\frac{F^pH^n(K^\bullet)}{F^{p+1}H^n(K^\bullet)},
$$

using $\ker g=\operatorname{im}\alpha$. The isomorphism is induced by
$\iota$, compatibly with $g$, which is the convergence of
[def-sp-convergence] to the image filtration
[def-sp-image-filtration]. This is (b).

Step 4: functoriality. A morphism of filtered complexes maps the short exact
sequences of Step 1 to each other, so it induces maps on
$H(F^pK^\bullet)$ and $H(\operatorname{gr}^pK^\bullet)$ which commute with
the maps induced by inclusions and projections and, by naturality of the
connecting homomorphism, with $f$; that is a morphism of exact couples, and
[lem-sp-couple-morphism] turns it into a morphism of spectral sequences. If it
is an isomorphism on $E_1$, it is an isomorphism on every page by
[lem-sp-page-induction]. This is (c).

Step 5: the first-quadrant variant. If $E_1^{p,q}=0$ outside the first
quadrant, so are all later pages, which are subquotients of $E_1$. On page
$r$ the differential leaving $(p,q)$ lands in $(p+r,q-r+1)$, outside the
quadrant once $r>q+1$, and the one arriving comes from $(p-r,q+r-1)$,
outside once $r>p$; so for $r>\max(p,q+1)$ the entry $(p,q)$ is stable, and
the pages $r\geq2$ form a first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence. If
moreover $F^0H^n=H^n$ and $F^{n+1}H^n=0$, the isomorphisms
$E_\infty^{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pH^{p+q}(K^\bullet)$ of (b) for
$0\leq p\leq n$ exhibit $\bigl(H^n(K^\bullet)\bigr)_{n\geq0}$, with the
induced filtrations, as the abutment. This is (d).
